issues.t: Lower intake manifold gasket coolant leak
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping, a puddle under the front, a temperature warning light, stalling or hard starting, and sometimes milky oil.
issues.why: The 3.4L V6 intake manifold gaskets break down and leak coolant outside the engine or into the oil. Owners report failures from about 57,000 to 104,000 miles, and some leaked again after a repair.
issues.next: Keep the coolant full and watch the temperature gauge. Get the gaskets replaced soon, because coolant in the oil can ruin the engine.

issues.sym: Overheating, coolant loss, white exhaust smoke or rough running.
issues.why: Head gaskets fail on the Aztek's 3.4L V6, sometimes as early as about 39,000 miles and often after a coolant leak or overheating.
issues.next: Stop driving if it overheats. Have a cooling system pressure test and combustion leak test done before the heads warp.

issues.sym: Slipping, harsh or missing shifts, or the transmission quitting outright.
issues.why: Owners report transmission failures at about 63,000 to 112,000 miles, and some replacement units failed again.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. If it slips, avoid hard driving and get a transmission diagnosis before more damage is done.

issues.t: Erratic shifting from pressure control solenoid
issues.sym: Shifts feel harsh, late or random.
issues.why: A failing pressure control solenoid inside the transmission can't hold line pressure steady. RepairPal lists it as the most common Aztek problem.
issues.next: Have the codes and line pressure checked. Replacing the solenoid early can prevent a full rebuild.

issues.t: Body control module and wiring faults
issues.sym: Intermittent no-start, gauges, radio and lights shutting off while driving, dead batteries, locks and hatch release not working, and random warning chimes.
issues.why: Owners trace these faults to a failing body control module (BCM), and in one case a wiring harness rubbing through on an ABS bracket. Bad grounds were also reported.
issues.next: Have the battery and charging system tested first, then ask for a check of the BCM codes and the wiring near the ABS bracket.

issues.sym: The rear hatch won't open with the fob or the inside button.
issues.why: Owners report this from 14,000 to 117,000 miles. It's an electrical fault; disconnecting the battery for a while fixed it for one owner.
issues.next: Check the fuse, then try a battery reset. If it keeps happening, have the release switch, latch motor and body module checked.

issues.t: Anti-theft system locks out the engine
issues.sym: The security light comes on and the engine won't start, or starts and dies.
issues.why: The anti-theft system can mistake the key for a wrong one and disable starting.
issues.next: Try waiting 10 minutes with the key on, then restart. A repeat problem needs the ignition cylinder and theft system tested.

issues.sym: The gas gauge stops working, sticks on full, or the low fuel light comes on with fuel in the tank.
issues.why: Owners report inaccurate or dead fuel gauges, usually from the fuel level sender in the tank.
issues.next: Track your mileage so you don't run dry, and have the fuel level sender tested.

issues.sym: The key won't turn fully off or won't come out, sometimes for hours, and the electrical system may stay on and drain the battery.
issues.why: Owners report it on early and late Azteks. The ignition switch or the shifter's park lock is the usual suspect; one new switch didn't fix it.
issues.next: Make sure the shifter is fully in Park. Have the shift interlock and ignition cylinder checked.

issues.sym: The A/C blows warm air or quits.
issues.why: A/C failure is one of the most reported Aztek complaints for these years, at around 75,000 miles on average.
issues.next: Have the system leak-tested and the compressor checked before a recharge.

issues.t: Heater and blower work only some of the time
issues.sym: The fan or heat comes and goes, or the blower quits.
issues.why: Owners report intermittent blower and heater operation. A blower motor or resistor is the usual cause.
issues.next: Have the blower motor, resistor and connector checked; a melted connector is common on GM blowers.

issues.sym: A growl or hum that changes with speed or when turning.
issues.why: Front wheel hub bearings wear out, sometimes around 40,000 miles and sometimes more than once.
issues.next: Have the bearings checked. A badly worn bearing can get hot and affect steering and ABS.

issues.t: Loud cracking noise from the rear brakes
issues.sym: A loud cracking or grinding noise from the rear when braking.
issues.why: Owners report rust and rotor problems at high mileage that keep coming back after repairs.
issues.next: Have the rear brakes inspected for rust, sticking slides and worn parts.

issues.t: Gas smell or leak from cracked fuel tank or filler
issues.sym: A gasoline smell inside or outside, or fuel dripping near the filler tube.
issues.why: Owners report cracks in the plastic tank and filler neck, and one fire after fuel sprayed onto the exhaust.
issues.next: Don't drive with a fuel smell or drip. Park outside and have the tank inspected; check for the fuel tank recall too.

issues.t: Fuel tank inlet valve weld can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell or fuel drops on the side of the tank.
issues.why: The weld on the fuel tank inlet check valve could crack and leak fuel, a fire risk.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup or call a GM dealer. If the work was never done, the dealer does it free.

issues.t: Engine may not restart from ignition relay (recall)
issues.sym: After you shut the engine off, it may not restart right away.
issues.why: A contaminated ignition relay could stop the engine from restarting, which could leave you stranded in traffic.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup or call a GM dealer. If the work was never done, the dealer does it free.

issues.sym: Steering may feel loose or not respond.
issues.why: The intermediate steering shaft could spin inside its coupling and cause a loss of steering control.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup or call a GM dealer. If the work was never done, the dealer does it free.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may be missing a pin (recall)
issues.why: A missing check valve pin could make the passenger airbag less protective.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup or call a GM dealer. If the work was never done, the dealer does it free.

issues.t: Child seat anchors may not be attached (recall)
issues.sym: No warning; a child seat clipped to the LATCH anchors may not be held properly.
issues.why: The child seat anchor wires on some vehicles were not attached correctly.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup or call a GM dealer. If the work was never done, the dealer does it free. Use the seat belt to install child seats until it is checked.
